name: Can I stay in my house during a kitchen addition, or do I need to move out?

mainEntity.name: Can I stay in my house during a kitchen addition, or do I need to move out?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A temporary kitchen can work when the project is properly phased, but an occupied-home expansion still creates dust, noise, access restrictions, and utility interruptions. Elite Remodeling & Design can discuss sequencing and site coordination during planning.

**Context:** Keeping part of the kitchen active may reduce convenience but extend the schedule or limit demolition access. Closing the full kitchen may shorten some phases while requiring a stronger temporary setup.

**Key factors:**
- Which walls and utilities are being altered
- Safe separation between living and work areas
- Material storage and delivery access
- Household schedule and occupant needs

**Practical guidance:** Decide whether speed or continued partial use matters more. Ask for a site-protection plan covering dust barriers, daily cleanup, material storage, pets, children, and access to the rest of the home.

A realistic occupancy plan reduces stress and protects finished areas.
acceptedAnswer.description: Many homeowners remain in the house, but the decision depends on demolition, utility interruptions, dust, noise, access, and household needs. Ask Elite Remodeling & Design for a site-protection and phasing plan, then decide whether partial occupancy is practical.
